item.title: Brazil: Amazon deforestation at 40-year low
item.description:
Brazilians filling out presidential ballots earlier this month saw three-term incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva pitted against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Environmental observers saw something else: a referendum on the future of the Amazon rainforest. “We are very serious about the risks for the Amazon if Flávio wins the election, because he is a climate denier,” said Carlos Nobre, a climate scientist currently at the University of São Paulo’s Institute for Advanced Studies. “If this candidate is elected, certainly deforestation in the Amazon will increase. We are in a very serious situation.” Flávio Bolsonaro, son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, is campaigning on an agribusiness-friendly, deregulatory agenda . item.title: Oregon father is the latest armed civilian to confront a gunman in a U.S. mass shooting
item.description:
A teacher threw her cellphone at a teenage gunman and tackled him during Thursday’s deadly shooting at an Oregon elementary school, fighting to wrestle away his shotgun before an armed father shot him dead, police revealed Friday . The 16-year-old gunman killed four people, including three children, at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, where he had previously been a special needs student. All of the victims were in a special-needs classroom, school officials said. The teacher was not injured in the confrontation. Her heroic actions “almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed,” Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said during a news conference detailing the attack. The father, identified as Kaylub Giamanco , 36, has two children at the school. He witnessed the initial shooting outside and followed the gunman into the school, police said. item.title: Mexico sentences killers of US, Australian surfers to 158 years each in prison
item.description:
Three men in Mexico received 158-year prison sentences Friday for the murders of Australian surfers Callum and Jake Robinson and their American friend Carter Redd Rhoad. A federal judge in the town of Ensenada, Baja California sentenced Jesús Gerardo García, Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús each to 158 years and nine months in prison for murder, robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence. An accomplice of García's — Ary Gisell Silva Raya — was also convicted of aggravated robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence and sentenced to 20 years in November after agreeing to an abbreviated trial. item.title: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia show the Yemeni rebels' growing strength
item.description:
The deadliest week for civilians in the Gulf marks a turning point in the US-Iran war that has engulfed the Middle East from Beirut to Aden, and from Irbil to Salalah . Saudi Arabia stepped up strikes on Yemen’s Houthis after the group hit Riyadh’s airport 20 times this month, killing 17 people and injuring 333 . Despite Riyadh’s considerable air defenses and vast military spending, the militants have been able to outsmart the systems using relatively cheap drones and missiles. Iranian attacks on the Gulf have brought the region closer together, and the latest strikes by Tehran’s allies in Yemen have galvanized support for Saudi Arabia. Authorities in the region are reinforcing this message of unity: In today’s Friday prayer sermons in Kuwait, imams were instructed to praise the kingdom’s support during Iraq’s 1990 invasion and condemn the Houthis .
